## Purpose and Platform Shape
PortKiller is a native, cross-platform developer desktop utility for discovering listening TCP ports, terminating owning processes, monitoring selected ports, managing Kubernetes `kubectl port-forward` sessions, and inspecting Cloudflare Tunnel activity. Platforms are independently implemented rather than sharing a UI layer: Swift/SwiftUI on macOS, C#/WPF on Windows, and Python on Linux. A Rust core exists for Linux-oriented process/scanner primitives.

## Application Entry Points
- macOS app bootstrap and composition root: `platforms/macos/Sources/PortKillerApp.swift`; central observable application state: `platforms/macos/Sources/AppState.swift`.
- Windows WPF startup and primary shell: `platforms/windows/PortKiller/App.xaml`, `platforms/windows/PortKiller/MainWindow.xaml`.
- Linux Python startup coordinates configuration, scanning, services, and UI: `platforms/linux/src/main.py`.
- Rust library boundary for reusable low-level scanning/process behavior: `portkiller-core/src/lib.rs`.

## Port Discovery and Process Control
Port scanning is the foundational data flow: OS inspection produces port/process records, which are filtered, categorized, rendered, and acted upon. macOS encapsulates scanning behind `platforms/macos/Sources/PortScanner.swift` and its protocol at `platforms/macos/Sources/Protocols/PortScannerProtocol.swift`; port domain data lives in `platforms/macos/Sources/Models/PortInfo.swift`. Windows separates scan and kill operations into `platforms/windows/PortKiller/Services/PortScannerService.cs` and `platforms/windows/PortKiller/Services/ProcessKillerService.cs`. Linux implements scanning in `platforms/linux/src/scanner.py`, with Rust alternatives in `portkiller-core/src/scanner/linux.rs` and `portkiller-core/src/process/linux.rs`.

## State, Persistence, and Monitoring
macOS concentrates user-driven lifecycle behavior in AppState extensions: refresh, favorites, watched ports, annotations, keyboard shortcuts, and process operations are split across `platforms/macos/Sources/AppState+AutoRefresh.swift`, `platforms/macos/Sources/AppState+WatchedPorts.swift`, and `platforms/macos/Sources/AppState+PortOperations.swift`. Persistent user preferences are abstracted through storage protocols and defaults-backed implementations, e.g. `platforms/macos/Sources/Protocols/StorageProtocols.swift` and `platforms/macos/Sources/Services/Storage/DefaultsWatchedPortsStorage.swift`. Windows equivalents are MVVM state plus settings service: `platforms/windows/PortKiller/ViewModels/MainViewModel.cs` and `platforms/windows/PortKiller/Services/SettingsService.cs`.

## Kubernetes Port-Forwarding Subsystem
macOS has the most developed port-forwarding subsystem. `platforms/macos/Sources/Managers/KubernetesDiscoveryManager.swift` discovers Kubernetes resources; `platforms/macos/Sources/Managers/PortForwardManager.swift` owns saved connection lifecycle, while `platforms/macos/Sources/Managers/PortForwardProcessManager.swift` executes and monitors child `kubectl` processes. Process output crosses through `platforms/macos/Sources/Services/PortForwardOutputParser.swift`, producing connection models in `platforms/macos/Sources/Models/PortForwardConnection.swift`. The dedicated UI begins at `platforms/macos/Sources/Views/PortForwarder/PortForwarderWindowView.swift`.

## Cloudflare, OS Services, and External Boundaries
Cloudflare support discovers and manages local `cloudflared` processes rather than exposing a server API boundary: macOS uses `platforms/macos/Sources/Services/CloudflaredDiscoveryService.swift`, `platforms/macos/Sources/Managers/TunnelManager.swift`, and `platforms/macos/Sources/Managers/NamedTunnelManager.swift`; Windows uses `platforms/windows/PortKiller/Services/TunnelService.cs`; Linux uses `platforms/linux/src/services/cloudflare.py`. Other OS boundaries include clipboard, notifications, process execution, and permissions, represented by `platforms/macos/Sources/Services/ProcessExecutor.swift` and `platforms/macos/Sources/Services/PermissionService.swift`.

## Native Presentation and Delivery
macOS SwiftUI renders the main port table, menu-bar status UI, tunnel UI, and onboarding from `platforms/macos/Sources/Views/MainWindowView.swift`, `platforms/macos/Sources/Views/MenuBar/MenuBarView.swift`, and `platforms/macos/Sources/Views/CloudflareTunnels/CloudflareTunnelsView.swift`. Windows uses WPF views backed by ViewModels, including `platforms/windows/PortKiller/CloudflareTunnelsView.xaml`. Linux provides a tray/window UI in `platforms/linux/src/ui/tray.py` and `platforms/linux/src/ui/window.py`. CI, release, and platform packaging are driven by `.github/workflows/release.yml`, macOS `platforms/macos/Package.swift`, and Linux `platforms/linux/install.sh`.
